feature: First original drawing-list key resolves different depths in primary-object removal
evidenceType: Bounded static inspection of supplied pinned3.58f PE. No Windows target execution. Native VCMI fixture corroborates the port, not original Windows execution.

observations.claim: Clear8x6 signed-byte depths. A nonzero template priority flag leaves all cells at zero. Otherwise traverse columns from the anchor leftward and rows upward; begin each column at1, reset to1 on a blocked cell above a passable cell, inherit previous-column depth on a passable cell beside a blocked previous-column cell, write then increment.
Draw entry byte3 stores the per-tile depth from that table. The first two bytes are drawing index, byte2 packs the local offsets.

Draw insertion first compares signed byte3; strictly greater new depth appends after the last lower-depth entry. Smaller depths scan earlier. Equal depths additionally compare occlusion across the rectangles.
Primary selection scans the tile draw list in reverse within each original priority phase.

implementationBoundary: Among candidates in the first nonempty phase, select a unique maximum depth. Only the depth needed at the queried tile is computed. Preserve the previous unique-candidate path. Equal highest depths remain rejected; secondary occlusion order is not guessed.
limitations: Equal maximum depths in zc3-0 rock removal still need original secondary draw ordering.
This does not establish campaign battles or later scenario victories.
